newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES TRADE WEAK, HALT REBOUND.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES TRADE WEAK, HALT REBOUND.

text.p: Greek stocks turned back in early Thursday trade, bringing to a halt a 100-point rebound in the previous two sessions and brokers said the market was steadying before resuming the uptrend in July.
"Following the market's forcefull reaction at 1,450 points which added 100 points in two days, the market is now stabilising," said Costas Feggos, managing director of Axon Securities.
"It will move sideways within a trading range in the near-term, gathering momentum for a sustained appreciation which from July onwards may become more aggressive," he added.
The recent 300-point correction was deeper than expected as investors rushed to lock in substantial gains produced by this year's rally, exacerbating the selling pressure he said.
But the outlook remained positive as the government was expected to step up is efforts to foster the equities market.
"With large rights issues in key stocks such as National Bank and Intracom there are substantial reasons to believe that the government will not agitate the positive market climate," he said.
Technical analysts said that a substantial increase in turnover was a prerequisite for the market to clear resistance at 1,600 points and that a buy signal had not been given yet.
"It would take a significant increase in turnover to top the 1,600 level where there is considerable resistance," said Commercial Securities in a technical analysis report.

On Wendesday, Salomon Brothers said in its June global equity strategy report that Greek equities were overbought and expected to remain at current levels in the short-term following this year's rally.
Salomon also anticipated Athens to continue outperforming emerging market indices on continuing positive results from sound macroeconomic policies.
It said industrial stocks would outperform banks reversing current price differential trends.
The Athens general index was off 1.40 percent or 21.66 points to 1,521.88 from Wednesday's 1,542.11, after 35 minutes of trading.
Turnover amounted to 6.7 billion drachmas on volume of 2.1 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 94 to 52 with 23 shares unchanged on 169 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted at London's SEAQ International market at $11.10-$11.60. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,101-1,131 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,059-1,119 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying instrument were off 230 drachmas at 6,220.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 511.30-543.93 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $75.14-$76.84. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,124-3,338 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $13.18-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 215-246 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 **** Users
